gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Sony WH-1000XM6's mic stops working on its supplied cable, so on a PC it can only take calls over Bluetooth HFP. It also doesn't state that the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) only gained USB-C wired PC calls with firmware 8.2.20 (10 Feb 2026), which works 'only by certain VoIP applications'; earlier units shipped on 5.0.20.
standout_why: I compared against the cited SoundGuys 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (2026-10-22). It lists 'No USB listening' as a con for the Sony WH-1000XM6. It says the Jabra Evolve3 85 comes in a Teams version and a Zoom/Google Meet version with a USB-C adapter. It says the different, Aug-2026 Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) can take calls over USB-C. It never says the XM6 mic is dead on the 3.5 mm cable, that PC calls on the XM6 must use HFP/HSP, or that the QC Ultra (2nd Gen) needs firmware 8.2.20+ for USB-C calls and excludes consoles. I could not compare the RTINGS phone-call list (cited in chat 1) or What Hi-Fi (cited in chat 2) because only the navigation loaded, so I can't rule out that those pages mention it.
decides: This splits ChatGPT's top two picks for someone who wants to plug into a laptop for Zoom or Teams. The Sony WH-1000XM6 stays a Bluetooth-only headset for calls: plugging in the cable turns off Bluetooth, and Sony says to talk through the phone's mic. The Bose QC Ultra (2nd Gen) works as a wired USB-C headset with a mic on a PC once updated to 8.2.20 or later, though not with every app and not on consoles. The Jabra Evolve3 85 does PC calls through its included Link 390 dongle, but the box has to say MS or UC to match your platform. For phone calls and music the Sony pick still holds. For a wired desk setup, the Bose (updated) or the Jabra wins.

findings.label: Bluetooth while the supplied headphone cable is plugged in
findings.value: Off. Sony: 'When using the headphone cable, the Bluetooth function cannot be used.'
findings.source_title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Using the supplied headphone cable

findings.label: Headset microphone over the cable
findings.value: Not used. For a call while wired, Sony says to 'Answer the call using your smartphone, and talk using the microphone of the phone,' and to turn off Speak-to-Chat
findings.source_title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Using the supplied headphone cable
findings.note: Same page. When the headset is off, the cable still plays music but noise canceling, Quick Attention and Speak-to-Chat don't work.

findings.label: Video calls on a computer: connection required
findings.value: Bluetooth only, using the HFP/HSP calling profile and not A2DP. Sony: 'If you select music playback connections, a video call may not be available.' Sony also says it 'may not be available' depending on the video-calling app
findings.source_title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Making a video call on your computer
findings.note: Step 1 on the page is 'Connect the headset to your computer via a Bluetooth connection.' USB is not mentioned.

findings.label: USB audio
findings.value: Not supported, per SoundGuys ('No USB listening' con)
findings.source_title: The best noise canceling headphones for work 2026 - SoundGuys
findings.note: Named reviewer. Sony's help-guide index has no USB-audio topic, and its specifications page lists only a 'DC 5 V / 1.5 A' power source with no terminal row.

findings.label: Multipoint limits
findings.value: 2 devices at once over Bluetooth. A third device that connects drops one of them. With 2 connected, 'you cannot end the first call' when a second call comes in. The Sony | Sound Connect app must be on one of the two devices to enable it
findings.source_title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Connecting the headset to 2 devices simultaneously (multipoint connection)

findings.label: Bluetooth version, profiles, codecs
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.3; A2DP/AVRCP/HFP/HSP plus TMAP/GMAP/PBP; SBC, AAC, LDAC, LC3
findings.note: LE Audio pairing is documented for Android smartphones (help-guide topic TP1001872731).

findings.label: Firmware that added USB-C wired calls on a PC
findings.value: 8.2.20, released 10 Feb 2026: 'USB voice call support for your PC … enables two-way USB audio connection with a PC.' Exclusion: 'supported only by certain VoIP applications and may not work with all communication software'
findings.source_title: Bose support: QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) – Updating your headphones
findings.note: Production started on firmware 5.0.20 (Sept 2025), so units still on that firmware have no USB mic until updated. Update through the Bose app or btu.bose.com (Windows 10/11, latest two macOS).

findings.label: Firmware 10.12.12 (8 Sept 2026) USB and LE Audio additions
findings.value: Game/chat balance over wired USB for 'compatible PCs and mobile devices', which 'excludes gaming consoles'; 'Improved wired USB communications compatibility with web conferencing applications'; LE Audio (beta) on 'compatible Android and Windows devices'
findings.source_title: Bose support: QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) – Updating your headphones
findings.note: macOS is not named for USB calls or LE Audio.

findings.label: USB-C audio format, Bluetooth version, and included cable
findings.value: USB audio at 16-bit, 44.1 or 48 kHz 'from compatible source files'; Bluetooth 5.4; 3.5 mm to 2.5 mm audio cable included; power adapter not included
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: The product page doesn't mention the 24-bit/48 kHz lossless that firmware 8.2.20 added (support page above).

findings.label: Price, Bose US store
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose

findings.label: PC dongle and certification by variant
findings.value: Ships with the Jabra Link 390 Bluetooth adapter, USB-A or USB-C by choice. Teams certification is 'variant dependent'. Jabra lists it as certified for Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Zoom
findings.note: Also 'SKU dependent': wireless charging pad and Teams LED notifications. Fast Pair is Android only.

findings.label: Multipoint, Bluetooth version, LE Audio
findings.value: 2 devices at once; up to 8 paired; Bluetooth 5.3; LE Audio yes

findings.label: Link 390 dongle variants and supported headsets
findings.value: Two variants, 'one for Microsoft Teams-certified devices and one for UC-certified devices'. Works with Evolve 65 SE/TE, Evolve2 Buds/55/65/65 Flex/75/85, Evolve3 75/85 and the Speak2 75 speakerphone. Plug-and-play with no drivers; firmware is updated through Jabra Direct
findings.note: The page shows the standalone Link 390 as 'Sold out'.
